the development of an innovative multimodal‐3D pipeline, which allows for a better understanding of bone repair/regeneration.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed pipeline could provide a new and powerful method for the analysis of tissue regeneration in bone.
this study represents a proof of principle that the multimodal approach can provide a more detailed and accurate description of bone regeneration than the traditional histology.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of μMRI and μMRI is a powerful tool in non‐destructive bone tissue investigation and could allow researchers to non‐destructive characterization of bone tissue regeneration.
we developed a pipeline to coregister μCT and μMR images of bone samples, to visualize and quantify different tissue types in a 3D meta‐structure.
the 3D‐multimodal imaging technique could be used as a non‐destructive alternative to histological analysis of bone tissue, with a potential application to bone regeneration studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multimodal approach can be applied to other bone regeneration processes.
the multimodal‐3D metastructures can be used as an intermediate step between histology and μCT to provide a more complete description of the bone regeneration processes.
μMRI and μMRI–μCT fusion can provide a 3D meta‐histology that could be exploited to improve the quality of information on bone regeneration.
